turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
I'd like to offer a supervised rewrite.
A rewrite for what? You haven't shown me a single thing, and if I take that now I'm admitting there was something to rewrite. What's your evidence?
You still haven't told me who decided on the zero, or what it's based on. I'm not leaving until you do.
Sorry. The rewrite would replace the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's procedure 4.4, and I'll want it in writing tonight. It still doesn't tell me why my son has a zero. What do you actually have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you offered Owen a supervised rewrite whose mark would replace the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still want to know who decided on the zero and on what evidence, and I want the zero withdrawn. I expect that commitment in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; your promise that the rewrite would replace the zero and nothing would go on his record met her one non-negotiable, but she still wants to know who decided on the zero and on what evidence, and still wants it withdrawn; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and she had not accepted it because no evidence was ever heard, with time left on her clock.
What moved her: You spelled out that the rewrite would replace the zero with nothing on his record, which matched the one thing she will never trade.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before showing any evidence, so taking it would have felt to her like admitting Owen did something.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you showed none; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking who decided on the zero and when, own in one sentence that it went into the gradebook before anyone called her, then put a dated document tied to Owen's own work in front of her before mentioning the rewrite.
Can you give me more detailed feedback? Like a full page?
